ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left figure is a cardiac muscle fiber action potential curve, with the horizontal axis as time (sec), marked with about 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 s; the curve rises rapidly near 0 s, then has a relatively long plateau phase, and finally rapidly falls near 0.30 s and returns to near the resting potential. The right figure shows the changes in relative permeability of different ions over time. Reasoning: The question asks for the approximate duration of the cardiac muscle fiber action potential, so the horizontal span from the beginning of the rapid rise to the end of repolarization in the left action potential should be read. This span extends approximately from 0 s to 0.30 s, therefore the duration is about 0.30 seconds.

Read the question text as asking for the approximate duration of this cardiac fiber action potential. Measure the horizontal span of the waveform from the upstroke to the end of repolarization; it is about 0.30 seconds. Return 0.30 secs.
